scope.flow: GaugeV2 reward accrual and distribution when total staked supply is zero

statements.text: Users withdraw or withdrawAll all staked tokens from the gauge, setting _totalSupply to zero.
Time passes without any deposits while total supply is zero.
During the empty period, notifyRewardAmount may be called by the distribution contract to add new rewards.
rewardPerToken is invoked while _totalSupply == 0 and returns the stored value without adding time-based accrual.
The updateReward modifier advances lastUpdateTime to the current applicable time regardless of supply.
New deposits occur and users interact with the gauge after the empty period.
Because rewardPerToken skips accrual at zero supply while lastUpdateTime advances, the empty period's emissions are never accrued and future calculations do not retroactively include them.
Reward tokens transferred to the contract during the empty period never become claimable by users.
When the gauge remains empty for an entire reward duration (one week), the full epoch's emissions become permanently unclaimable and stuck in the contract.
Entire epochs of reward emissions can become permanently stuck, leading to protocol fund loss without recovery, with higher impact in low-liquidity gauges that frequently empty.
Rewards emitted during a period, including periods of zero total supply, should be accrued and remain claimable rather than being skipped when lastUpdateTime advances.
The report assumes skipped emissions cannot be recovered by any later notifyRewardAmount or interaction.

ambiguities: Report does not state who triggers the updateReward modifier during the empty period or whether notifyRewardAmount itself invokes it.
No explicit numeric rewardRate, duration, or emission amounts are given beyond the one-week duration.
Whether the skipped rewards are truly unrecoverable versus recoverable via later notifications is asserted but not demonstrated.
No unauthorized-caller or access-control condition is claimed; distribution contract role is only described as possibly calling notifyRewardAmount.
